editorial_note: A field is present only if an official page stated it. A field is null when no official source stated it. `listing_only: true` means the value came from the Amazon detail page and should be re-checked against the manufacturer page before any marketing claim.

flags.title: Preset count contradicts itself on the manufacturer's own page
flags.detail: The Emeril Everyday product page shows a spec tile reading '25 Cooking Pre-sets' while the product body copy on the same page says '24 one-touch cooking presets'. The Amazon listing title says '24 One-Touch Preset Options'. No official page resolves the discrepancy, so the field is blank on the site and no preset count is claimed anywhere in the copy.
flags.action: Ask the manufacturer which figure is current; then publish that number with the source date.

flags.title: Amazon listing names a different model number than the manufacturer page
flags.detail: The Amazon 'About this item' block for B08DKYBTPH ends with '1000 Watts/120 Volts – RJ38-SQSS-8T', while the CHEFMAN product page for RJ38-SQSS-8T states 1700W/120V and 400 F. The wattage figure contradicts itself between the two official pages. The site publishes the manufacturer's 1700 W and flags the conflict; the wattage should not be used in ad copy until confirmed.
flags.action: Confirm wattage with CHEFMAN support in writing before any paid or comparison claim.

flags.title: None of the five supplied links carries the tracking ID
flags.detail: Each supplied link is a link.amazon short URL with a 9-character code. Resolving them yields amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> URLs with no tag= parameter. Under Program Policies section 2(b), the Associates ID must appear as a parameter in the URL of each link placed on a site, and under the Agreement section 1 links must use the tagged link formats Amazon provides. As supplied, these links would not attribute commission to shopnow047c-20. The exact compliance status of link.amazon short links is not addressed in the documents reviewed — do not describe them as invalid; describe them as untagged and unresolved.
flags.action: Re-issue all five links from Associates Central SiteStripe with tag=shopnow047c-20, or enroll them in the Associates workflow and confirm the tracking report before scaling.

flags.title: Link 4 resolves to no product
flags.detail: https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 lands on an Amazon 'Continue shopping' interstitial on repeated attempts. A direct catalog search for B0C8MOW59 returns 'No results for your search query'. No product name, brand, or specification is published for slot 4, because none could be confirmed. Note also that the code contains a lowercase letter and is 9 characters, so it is not in the standard 10-character ASIN format.

flags.title: Battery life differs between two CHEF iQ pages
flags.detail: The iQ Sense product page advertises '70+ Hours of Battery'. The iQ Sense FAQ states Gen 3 probes hold a charge for up to 60 hours. Both are on chefiq.com. The product register records the marketing figure and this note; no single number is asserted in buyer-facing copy.
flags.action: Ask CHEF iQ which figure applies to the 3-probe Gen 3 bundle.

flags.detail: The Emeril Everyday product page states 7 accessories are included. The manufacturer's own accessory page states the grill plate 'is now an optional accessory and is no longer included'. Retail listings still describe a set including a grill plate. Nothing on the site claims a specific accessory list; the copy says to check the current box contents.
